result.topic_en: Hilbert notes that the zeta function can be written as an integral of a product of two functions each satisfying a linear second-order differential equation, asks for the fundamental solutions of certain third-order heat-type equations, and records leftover remarks on integral equations concerning spectral representations of quadratic forms in infinitely many variables.

items.quote:
Wie heissen die Grundlösungen von $\frac{d^3u}{dx^3}+\frac{\partial u}{\partial y}=0$ ?, $\frac{d^3u}{dx^3}+\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial y^2}+\frac{\partial u}{\partial z}=0$
nach Analogie der Wärmeleitungsgl. $\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2}+\frac{\partial u}{\partial y}=0$, wo man nach
Funktionen $u$, die nur von $\frac{y^2}{x}$ abhängen!
items.english: What are the fundamental solutions of $u_{xxx}+u_y=0$?, $u_{xxx}+u_{yy}+u_z=0$, by analogy with the heat equation $u_{xx}+u_y=0$, where one [looks] for functions $u$ that depend only on $y^2/x$!

items.quote:
Die Frage der Max. und Min. einer quadratischen Form mit unendlich
vielen Variabeln lässt sich durch die (Partialbruchdarstellung) Spektraldarstellung
allgemein beantworten.
items.english: The question of the maxima and minima of a quadratic form in infinitely many variables can be answered in general by the (partial fraction representation) spectral representation.

items.quote:
Wenn
die Faltung von $K(\lambda;a,[-...-].)\,K(\lambda;a.)$ bei Annäherung von $\lambda$ an
einen Punkt $\nu$ endlich bleibt, so sind die inhomogenen aus [-...-]
$(x'x)-\nu K(x)$ entspringenden Gleichungen stets lösbar.
items.english: If the convolution of $K(\lambda;a,.)K(\lambda;a.)$ remains finite as $\lambda$ approaches a point $\nu$, then the inhomogeneous equations arising from $(x'x)-\nu K(x)$ are always solvable.
